analysis.title: End of Week Market Intelligence: dc downside?
key_insights: S&P 500 is on pace for a ~2% weekly loss as of Friday 11:45AM ET. The VIX spiked to 28 on Thursday and was 24 on Friday. GS ties the volatility mainly to concern that opposition to data center development could widen the supply-demand gap in the data center supply chain.

The core debate is whether the compute that has been ordered (semiconductors, servers, fiber optic cables) will have a place to be installed when delivered. The midterm elections raise the chance of short-term state-level moratoriums on data center construction, per Hatzius and Phillips.
Capacity (Mike Ng): GS's already-conservative forecast of 20 GW-IT of data center capacity coming on in 2027 is still on track. The forecast rises to 24 GW in 2028 and falls to 23 GW-IT in 2029.

Construction (Adam Bubes): all projects in GS's 2027 forecast have already broken ground. Only about half of the 2028 projects on the watch list have broken ground, so part of the 2028 forecast could be delayed by state-level moratoriums.

Electricity (Carly Daventport): Democratic wins could increase near-term uncertainty around data center development, particularly in Texas and Georgia. GS still sees those markets as important longer-term areas for load growth and flags potential risk to Texas-exposed stocks including NRG and VST.

Financing (Amanda Lynam): hyperscalers are on pace to finance 36% of their capex this year with credit, and GS forecasts 35% in 2027. Only 43% of the $687bn of financing seen this year is from hyperscalers. State-level moratoriums could affect ~45% of planned US data center capacity, with Texas alone 25%.

October payrolls were much better than expected at +165k, and the unemployment rate fell 10bp to 4.1%. Upward revisions to the two prior months lifted the three-month average to 137k from 51k before the report. GS's underlying job growth estimate is 124k, up from 51k.

GS reads the payrolls report as evidence that AI's impact on employment so far is still muted. It cites a Pierfrancesco Mei note that workers displaced from AI-exposed jobs outside tech take longer to find new jobs, and that the new jobs are as vulnerable to AI displacement or more so.

Fiscal: Johan Allen and Joseph Briggs caution that large deficits pose growth risks, since deficit levels in France, the US and the UK have often triggered fiscal consolidation. Mei says it is less disruptive to cut spending voluntarily before markets or an outside authority force it.

Business sentiment was mixed: Manufacturing ISM rose above expectations and Services ISM ticked down. September construction spending was well below expectations. UMich consumer sentiment improved and inflation expectations declined.

GS says high-volatility periods usually bring rising stock correlation, but this one is centered on the AI trade. It recommends stock picking outside AI. GS added APH (cable and connectors, significant data center construction exposure) to its US Conviction List in the November update.

GS has 13 X-AI stocks (not linked to the AI trade) on the US Conviction List: BURL, DAL, EL, ORLY, VIK (consumer), CFG (regional bank), UNH and VRTX (healthcare), CSL, CWST, HII and UPS (industrials), and OXY (E&P oil turnaround).

Next week: October CPI on Tuesday and PPI on Friday, plus Existing Home Sales and a small business sentiment survey. Earnings from AI-sensitive NRG and AMAT, and from X-AI names OXY, TDG, KKR and TTWO.

tension_points.bull_case: GS's already-conservative forecast of 20 GW-IT of capacity in 2027 is on track, and all projects in the 2027 forecast have already broken ground.
tension_points.bear_case: Only about half of the 2028 watch-list projects have broken ground. State-level moratoriums could affect ~45% of planned US capacity (Texas alone 25%), delaying part of the 2028 forecast.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A state-level moratorium on data center construction, including one in Texas, that delays 2028 projects not yet broken ground.
